Summary: Kent is right, he's offended. The notion of him being in love with Superman is downright ludicrous. It’d be preposterous to fall in love with the metahuman from a different life—a different world—and it would be impossible for him even to form something like a personal connection to the figure. But Kent clearly had a reason for wanting to believe that. He needed Bruce Wayne to have a motivation for being secretive and starting all his hidden donations, and somehow, the most plausible option to him was the possibility that the CEO of Wayne Enterprises was in love with the superhero known as Superman.   [Three years after the great Gotham flood, the ground shakes. Gotham's blood erupts from its cracks, and people with toxic, superhuman capabilities run amok. The line between Batman and Bruce Wayne blurs, and he searches desperately for an answer from the dazzling, seemingly perfect metahuman across the bridge. What ensues is a chase for the truth, both for the strange phenomenon plaguing the city and Batman's journey to admitting that he might need Superman more than he thinks he does.]
